title: Establish workload-class SLOs and automated rollback/degradation thresholds for inference endpoints
creator: Maya Gupta
description:
Background: We need a clear, workload-class based SLO framework for Redwood hosted inference endpoints that ties latency targets, availability bands, and error budgets to automated rollout/rollback rules. Current SLO work is scattered by product team and region. This ticket consolidates definitions for three workload classes (Interactive, Conversational, Batch) and specifies deterministic rollback and graceful-degradation thresholds that the Console and orchestration layer will enforce during canary and progressive rollouts.

Goal: Produce a concrete SLO matrix and a set of acceptance criteria that engineering can implement as enforceable rollout gates (percent-based canaries, automated throttling, and auto-rollback). Deliverables include an SLO table, a rollout-gate spec for the orchestration layer, synthetic validation tests, and a short playbook for on-call.

Non-goal: This ticket does not implement the orchestration mechanics; it defines the thresholds and test cases for implementation in a follow-up ENG ticket.
acceptance_criteria: SLO matrix created for three workload classes: Interactive, Conversational, Batch, with explicit latency P50/P95/P99 targets and availability targets (percent uptime), published to the Console SLO docs.
Error budget definitions and burn-rate policies documented for each workload class, including short-window detection (5/30/60 minute windows) and rolling 7-day view.

Automated rollback rules defined: clear predicate expressions (e.g., burn-rate > 5x for 30 minutes OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10 minutes) that can be implemented as feature flags/config in the rollout engine.

Progressive rollout plan with numeric thresholds (canary percentages and verification periods) for 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% that include mandatory health checks for latency, error rate, and CPU/GPU overload signals.
Synthetic test suite specified (load patterns, sample prompts, token lengths) that validates SLOs for canary traffic; tests runnable by the QA/CI pipeline and documented with pass/fail criteria.
Stakeholder sign-off recorded from Product, Infra/Serving, SRE, and Developer Experience teams before handoff to engineering.
Playbook for on-call included: exact steps for pause/rollback, targeted mitigations (reduce batch size, route to cheaper variants), and required postmortem artifacts when rollback is triggered.
All acceptance criteria are represented as discrete checklist items in the project board and marked Done before implementation work begins.
decisions: Adopt three workload classes (Interactive, Conversational, Batch) rather than per-model SLOs to reduce operational complexity.
Use percentile-based latency SLOs tied to request size buckets (short: <64 tokens, medium: 64-512, long: >512) to avoid incentive inversion.
Rollback predicates should combine both latency and error-budget signals to avoid noisy single-metric rollbacks.
Canary durations chosen to balance detection speed and false positives: 15 minutes for 1% canary, 30 minutes for 5%, 60 minutes for 25%.
Automated degradation actions allowed before full rollback: reduce max concurrency for canary, switch canary traffic to lower-cost model variant, and engage prefix cache bypass if indicated.
scope_changes: Initial scope included per-region SLO customization; deferred regional deviation to a separate follow-up ticket to keep this deliverable focused on global defaults.
Excluded private/Dedicated specific contractual SLO clauses; this ticket focuses on hosted API SLO defaults that Dedicated/Private PMs can import and adapt.
Added synthetic test definitions after feedback from SRE during review; tests were not in the original brief.
rollout_gates: Mandatory checks at each gate: p95 latency within 1.2x baseline for request-size bucket, error rate below configured error budget burn threshold, infra saturation (GPU mem/CPU) under 75%.
Auto-rollback trigger: error budget burn-rate > 5x baseline for a 30-minute window OR sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 10 minutes despite mitigation actions.

Soft-degradation actions: reduce concurrency, fall back to lower-cost model variant, enable KV-prefix cache where applicable; these must be executed automatically when burn-rate between 2x-5x for 20 minutes before full rollback.
Human-in-the-loop gate for releases that touch customer-facing billing/quotas: require SRE and product signoff prior to 25% stage.
metrics: Latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99) per request-size bucket and per model variant.
Availability (successful response rate excluding client cancel) over rolling 24h and 7d windows.
Error budget consumption rate (absolute errors divided by total requests) with burn-rate alarms for 5m/30m/1h windows.
Infrastructure signals: GPU utilization, GPU memory pressure, host CPU, and request queue latency.
Canary-specific metrics: time-series of metric deltas vs. baseline with automated anomaly scoring used for gate decisions.
